title: EU housing is split between houses and flats
content: Eurostat reported that in 2024, 51 percent of the EU population lived in a house and 48 percent in a flat, with substantial differences between countries.

title: Flats dominate EU city living
content: Eurostat reported that 73 percent of the EU city population lived in a flat in 2024, compared with 27 percent living in a house. City-focused security concepts should emphasize compact and shared-boundary contexts.

title: Germany has an unusually high tenant share
content: Eurostat reported that 53 percent of Germany's population were tenants in 2024, making Germany the only EU country in which renting was more common than ownership in that dataset.

title: GDPR requires purpose limitation and data minimisation
content: European Commission guidance states that organisations must process personal data for specific purposes and collect only the personal data necessary to fulfil those purposes.

title: EU Cyber Resilience Act sets lifecycle cybersecurity requirements
content: Regulation EU 2024/2847 establishes cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements and vulnerability-handling obligations for manufacturers during the expected period of use.

title: Housing costs make price assumptions region-sensitive
content: Eurostat reported that EU households spent an average of 19 percent of disposable income on housing in 2024. This macro indicator supports affordability sensitivity but does not directly measure security-device willingness to pay.

title: Shared-building security requires bystander-aware sensing
content: Apartment entry and corridor sensing may capture neighbors, visitors and delivery workers who are not product users. Field of view, retention and notification design should minimize bystander data.

title: Local processing can support privacy but does not ensure compliance
content: Processing events locally may reduce raw household data transfer and latency, but lawful purpose, access controls, retention and user rights still require explicit product design.

title: Country differences weaken a single Western Europe launch assumption
content: Housing tenure, dwelling type, channels and language differ across Germany, France and other European markets. A shared core product may still require country-specific installation, consent and go-to-market validation.

title: Retrofit products must expose a clear removal and data-exit path
content: Renter-oriented security hardware should be removable without major damage, while accounts and household data need understandable export or deletion paths when residents move.
